newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices flat to up 1/8 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices flat to up 1/8 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices opened flat to up 1/8 point amid pricing for a $540 million Puerto Rico Public Buildings Authority offering via Smith Barney Inc.
Thin supply was fostering municipals' strength, a trader said.

"You've got a lot of competitive deals that will be bid up very aggressively today, and very few negotiated deals," the trader said. "Everything has been bid up so high that the secondary has lagged a little, and now you've seen a lot of the primary guys coming to the secondary to buy bonds. So that's why we've seen the Blue List going down and down and down."
The trader judged the muni cash market up 1/8 point overall, and 1/4 point higher in spots.
A second trader said the market opened flat, but agreed competitive deals have been coming "fully priced."
"You've got a Blue List of $992 (million), so it's not like we don't need bonds, because we do," the trader said.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 3/32 at 97-11/32 to yield 6.83 percent. In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 1/32 a 116-13/32. The September T-bond contract was up 1/32 at 110-18/32. The MOB spread was 187 ticks.
In new issues, Morgan Stanley Dean Witter tentatively priced $243 million New York Local Government Assistance Corp bonds at a top yield of 5.40 percent in 2015.
Smith Barney Inc. tentatively priced the Puerto Rico deal at a top yield of 5.66 percent in 2021.
